samples.summary: Peer caret still resolved with hardcoded 'backward' while peer selection now honors the published affinity — the two can render one visual line apart
samples.evidence: `resolvePositionPixel(peer.position, 'backward', …)` at editor.ts:1561-1563 is unchanged, but the peer's `activeSelection` endpoints now carry `lineAffinity` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:994-999 → docs-view.tsx:232 → computeSelectionRects). For a peer whose caret sits at the start of a continuation line (offset == wrap boundary, affinity 'forward'), their highlight is now painted starting on line k+1 while their caret marker is still drawn at the end of line k. Before this change both used the backward reading, so they at least agreed. `PeerCursor.position` was also not widened to carry the field, so the data needed to fix it is discarded at the type boundary.

samples.summary: `start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` is a behavior change for every non-cell caller, not the 'historical reading' the comment claims
samples.evidence: The comment at selection.ts:255-259 says the defaults "keep the historical reading". That is true only of the cell-internal branch (which hardcoded forward/backward). The block branch previously fed no affinity to `positionToPagePixel`/`findPageForPosition`, which default to `'backward'` (pagination.ts:385). So every affinity-less caller now resolves the START of a range on the *next* visual line at a wrap boundary: search-match highlights (editor.ts:1640), spell-error underline rects (editor.ts:1676), and peer selections published by clients that do not send affinity. In the cases I traced the painted region is visually equivalent (the old reading just emitted an extra zero-width rect), but this is an unflagged change to shared, out-of-diff rendering paths and the justifying comment is wrong.
searchedFor: grep computeSelectionRects across packages/docs/test (only the new test exists)

samples.summary: shift+Up/Down overwrites the fresh per-hit affinity on `newPos` with the cursor's possibly-stale `lineAffinity`
samples.evidence: `focus: { ...newPos, lineAffinity: focusAffinity }` with `focusAffinity = this.cursor.lineAffinity` for vertical moves. In the normal path `moveVertical` returns `result` (which already carries the correct `lineAffinity` from `paginatedPixelToPosition`) and sets `this.cursor.lineAffinity = result.lineAffinity` at text-editor.ts:4208, so the override is a no-op. But several `moveVertical` exits return WITHOUT updating `cursor.lineAffinity` — the table-entry branches (4191-4205), the cell clamps (4153/4156) and `return pos` (4159, 4106) — so on those paths the spread-in fresh value (or absence of one) is replaced by the affinity of the line the caret was on BEFORE the move, and the selection focus can resolve one visual line off.

samples.summary: `activeCursorPos` now carries `lineAffinity` at runtime but its presence type was not extended (only `activeSelection` was), so the caret half of the feature is dropped at every consumer
samples.evidence: `updateCursorPos` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2968) accepts `lineAffinity`, `clampPosToModel` copies it through (966-967), and line 2999 publishes `activeCursorPos: clampedPos` — so the field is on the wire. `DocsPresence.activeCursorPos` (users.ts:21-24) is still `{blockId; offset}`, and `buildPeerCursors` (docs-view.tsx:226) forwards it into `PeerCursor.position`, which is likewise untyped for it. Net effect: the caret affinity is published but unreadable/unused, while the selection affinity is used — the asymmetry behind the peer caret/highlight disagreement above. Also note the local caret's authoritative affinity lives in `Cursor.lineAffinity`, not on `cursor.position`, so for keyboard-driven moves `pos.lineAffinity` is simply `undefined` here and nothing publishes the real value.

samples.summary: `anchorDocPosition`'s default silently changed from 'backward' to undefined, changing what `setCompositionStart` stores and what `resolveAnchoredDocPosition` now hands back
samples.evidence: The parameter default was `'backward'` and is now optional/undefined (line 918), and `setCompositionStart` (line 1204) was changed to rely on that default. Combined with the new `lineAffinity: anchor.lineAffinity` returns (1054, 1072, 1124), the composition anchor and any anchor created without an explicit argument now resolve back to a `DocPosition` with no affinity where they previously would have recorded `'backward'`. I could find no consumer that reads the composition anchor's affinity, so this looks inert today, but it is an unremarked semantic change to a stored anchor that the design doc (docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:105) documents as carrying the field.
searchedFor: grep anchorDocPosition call sites in packages/frontend/src

samples.summary: shift+Home hardcodes 'forward' even when the visual line start is the block's first line (offset 0)
samples.evidence: `focus: { ...newPos, lineAffinity: 'forward' }` is applied unconditionally, but `getVisualLineStart` returns offset 0 when the caret is on the block's first visual line, which is not a wrap boundary. `findPageForPosition`'s forward branch only skips a line when `charCount + lineChars === offset`, i.e. when the first line has zero characters — so this is harmless for ordinary text, but for any block whose first laid-out line measures zero chars the highlight start would be pushed onto the second line. `getWrapAffinity` (text-editor.ts:4087-4102) exists precisely to answer this question and is not used here.
